part_1a_deficiencies.description: The firm did not identify and test any controls over the unsatisfied performance obligations the issuer expected to be recognized as revenue within the next 12 months.
The firm did not identify and test any controls over the accuracy and completeness of the report used in the operation of a control over unsatisfied performance obligations.
The firm performed a substantive analytical procedure but did not determine whether the expectation was based on predictable relationships and used an unsupported threshold.
The firm sent a positive confirmation request to the custodian for certain pension plan assets which was returned with exceptions but did not evaluate the nature of these exceptions.
The firm identified deviations in control operation but did not evaluate the effect on operating effectiveness and excluded certain loans from testing population.
The firm identified differences in loan risk ratings but did not evaluate the effect on audit evidence and did not perform substantive procedures for excluded loans.
The firm did not evaluate the specific review procedures that control owners performed to assess the reasonableness of qualitative factors.
The firm did not evaluate specific review procedures for risk ratings and did not test controls over accuracy and completeness of loan information used in controls.
The firm did not identify and test any controls over the accuracy and completeness of issuer-prepared schedules used in control operation for unsatisfied performance obligations disclosure.
The firm used issuer-prepared schedules in substantive testing but did not test or test controls over the accuracy and completeness of these schedules.
The firm did not identify and evaluate a misstatement in a required disclosure under FASB ASC Topic 606.
The firm did not identify and test any controls that addressed whether inventory was counted with sufficient frequency in accordance with the issuer's cycle-count policy.
The firm did not obtain sufficient appropriate audit evidence that cycle-count procedures were sufficiently reliable to produce results substantially the same as a count of all items each year.
The firm did not perform procedures to test the accuracy and completeness of issuer-produced data used by specialists and did not evaluate relevance and reliability of external information.
The firm did not evaluate the reasonableness of significant assumptions used by the company's specialists.
The firm did not evaluate the specific review procedures that the control owner performed to assess the appropriateness of excluding certain costs.
The firm used operating results in substantive procedures but did not evaluate whether excluded costs were directly associated with the identified asset groups.
The firm did not evaluate whether the issuer's method to determine recoverability using cash-flow forecasts that excluded costs was in conformity with FASB ASC Topic 360.
The firm did not evaluate the specific review procedures that the control owner performed to determine comparative prices and identify items for follow-up.
The firm did not perform sufficient procedures to evaluate the issuer's presentation of certain assets as current assets beyond inquiring of management.
The firm did not extend audit procedures to certain journal entries it identified as having certain fraud risk characteristics.
The year the firm began serving consecutively as the company's auditor included in the audit report was incorrect.
The firm's communication of a critical audit matter did not accurately refer to the relevant financial statement accounts or disclosures.
For certain permissible tax services, the firm did not describe in writing the scope and/or fee structure when seeking pre-approval from the audit committee.
The firm did not describe in writing to the audit committee all relationships that may have been thought to bear on independence prior to accepting the audit.
